# A prose `=` above a @member tag hijacks its published default

## Context

Found while reviewing #19017 (@sloemo01, moving `Filter`'s operator list into its `@member` tag). That PR's new tag is 168 characters, 42% longer than the longest the docs pipeline had previously been handed, so I read `publishedMemberDefault` to check for truncation. There is none — but the function has a different defect, and it is currently firing.

`#19017` is **not** the cause and is **not** affected: its prose line contains no `=`. It is also the reason this was found, and it removed a live instance of the hazard, because the line it deleted contained `'=='`.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-20T00:12Z; no equivalent found. Memory Core rationale sweep on the symptom's nouns returned the adjacent green-run-certifies-nothing family but nothing on this function. Archive grep over `resources/content/issues/` found no prior filing.

**Scope correction, after reading `docletCompactJsdoc.spec.mjs` (see The Architectural Reality).** This ticket originally proposed fixing all three of the function's failure modes. Two of them are **already documented, deliberately pinned, and backed by `.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` §12**, which forbids the authored forms that reach them. Only the third — the one below — is undocumented, undefended and unknown. The scope is now that one.

## The Problem

[`buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/memberDefaults.mjs:28`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/memberDefaults.mjs#L28) re-derives an Array/Object member's published default from the raw comment text, because JSDoc's optional-parameter syntax `[name=default]` eats a trailing `]`:

```js
let defaultValue = item.comment.substr(item.comment.indexOf('=') + 1);

return defaultValue.substr(0, defaultValue.indexOf('\n'))
```

`indexOf('=')` searches the **entire comment block**, not the `@member` tag. Any `=` in the prose above the tag — most commonly a `=>` in an arrow or a `key => value` description — wins, and the published default becomes a slice of that prose.

Worst specimen: `Neo.plugin.Resizable`'s docblock reads *"Directions into which you want to drag => resize"*. The published default for `validDirections` is the string `"> resize"`.

### Reproducer

```bash
npm run generate-docs-json
node -e '
const arr = require("./docs/output/all.json");
for (const d of arr) {
  if (!d || d.kind !== "member" || !d.comment) continue;
  if (!((d.type && d.type.names) || []).some(n => /array|object/i.test(n))) continue;
  const tag = d.comment.search(/@member\b/), eq = d.comment.indexOf("=");
  if (tag > -1 && eq > -1 && eq < tag) {
    console.log(d.meta.filename + ":" + d.meta.lineno, d.name, "=>", JSON.stringify(d.defaultvalue));
  }
}'
```

The last four are the same mechanism landing on a falsy result rather than a prose fragment — the member documents with no default instead of a wrong one.

**Population, stated in words:** every doclet of `kind: member` whose type names include `array` or `object` and whose comment text contains an `=` at a lower index than `@member`. That is the whole class; there is no sampling.

## The Architectural Reality

The function's own docblock enumerates three edges and closes with *"every edge above is silent — nothing throws, and the docs build stays green."* Reading only that docblock is what made this ticket's first draft wrong, because two of those edges are **already covered**:

`test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/docletCompactJsdoc.spec.mjs` pins both, deliberately, against the real JSDoc parser:

- `:181` — `FORBIDDEN: a one-line array or object default empties the GENERATED default`
- `:233` — `` THE TRAP: a separate @default on an array or object publishes `/**` as the default ``, whose own comment says *"This arm exists because an earlier version of §12 recommended exactly this form."*

Those arms exist so `.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` §12 can forbid the authored forms that reach them. Repairing either one is a **guidelines change** — it would make a currently-forbidden form safe — and it belongs with §12's author, not inside a slice-anchor fix.

The prose-`=` edge is different in every way that matters: **no authored form triggers it** (the author writes a perfectly ordinary docblock), nothing forbids it, no spec covers it, and unlike the other two it produces a value that *looks* plausible rather than obviously broken.

## The Fix

One expression. The `=` search anchors at the tag instead of at the comment's start:

```diff
-let defaultValue = item.comment.substr(item.comment.indexOf('=') + 1);
+let defaultValue = item.comment.substr(item.comment.indexOf('=', item.comment.search(/@member\b/)) + 1);
```

`\b` keeps `@memberOf` from anchoring, so `@memberOf!` + `@default` doclets keep the third edge's behaviour. When no tag is present `search` returns `-1` and `indexOf('=', -1)` behaves as `indexOf('=', 0)`, so that path is unchanged too — both documented edges survive by construction rather than by luck.

Touched: `buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/memberDefaults.mjs` (the expression plus its docblock), and one new spec. No source docblock changes — the 19 comments above are correct JSDoc and the pipeline is what misreads them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `=` search anchors at the `@member` tag, word-bounded so `@memberOf` does not match.
- [x] A unit spec calls `publishedMemberDefault` directly rather than re-implementing it, covering: a prose `=>` above the tag, a prose `==`, a prose `key => value`, a value whose own contents contain `=` (`Filter`'s `'=='`, `'<='`, `'>='`), and the multiline bracket repair the function exists for.
- [x] The spec pins **both documented edges as unchanged** — a one-line block still publishes `''`, a `@memberOf!` + `@default` doclet still publishes `/**` — so a later widening of scope has to delete an assertion rather than drift past one.
- [x] The spec guards **its own fixture**: JSDoc normalises `{String[]}` to `Array.<String>` and the stage matches on `'array'`, so a fixture carrying the authored spelling falls straight through and every arm goes vacuous. This happened while writing it — six arms returned the parser sentinel — and the arm exists because it did.
- [x] Red-first, per arm rather than per suite: **3 failed / 7 passed** against the pre-fix source with no skipped arms, **10 passed** with the fix, **10 passed** again after restoring it. The spec carries no `describe.serial`, which is why the tally is complete.
- [x] One-variable control at the same head, `dev@3f3710df32`, on the generated `all.json`:

  | | dev | with the fix |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | prose-`=` hijack | **19** | **0** |
  | one-line block → `''` | 1 | 1 |
  | `@default` → `/**` | 2 | 2 |
  | trailing-comma brackets | 4 | 4 |

- [x] `npm run generate-docs-json` green; the whole `buildScripts` unit tier green (**788 passed**); `docletCompactJsdoc.spec.mjs` green (**10 passed**).

## Out of Scope

- **The two documented edges**, per The Architectural Reality. Their live instances are `TopologyLibrary.mjs:94` / `PerspectiveLibrary.mjs:413` (`lastErrors=[]` in a one-line block) and `DefaultConfig.mjs` `config.mainThreadAddons` / `config.themes` (`@memberOf!` + `@default`). Those are §12 violations in source, and the interesting question — whether the pipeline should be repaired so §12 can loosen — is worth its own ticket with §12's author.
- **Four docblocks with a stray trailing comma**, which publish a comma inside the default: `form/FormContainer.mjs:22`, `form/Container.mjs:26`, `form/Fieldset.mjs:24`, `tab/Container.mjs:69`, all `baseCls`. Pre-existing, unaffected by this change, verified identical on both sides of the control.
- **`plugin/Resizable.mjs:27`**, whose docblock is tagged `@member {String[]} validDirections` while the member it documents is `static positions` on the next line. After this fix it publishes the right array under the wrong name.
- **Why `Neo.collection.Filter#operators` is not published as a member doclet at all** while 54 other protected-static array members are. Noticed here, unexplained, not load-bearing.
- **The unit tier's `describe.serial` habit.** 35 files on `dev`; 0 of 131 e2e and 0 of 2 visual. Captured as a defect-note; measured evidence in the #19015 review.

## Avoided Traps

- **Rewriting the 19 docblocks to remove their `=` characters.** That treats the symptom, costs 19 files, and leaves the next `=>` armed. The prose is good prose; *"Directions into which you want to drag => resize"* is clearer than any `=`-free paraphrase.
- **Fixing all three edges because all three are wrong.** Two are load-bearing documentation of forbidden forms. A fix that silently made them work would have left §12 forbidding something safe, and broken three arms that exist to say so.
- **A balanced-bracket scan instead of the line terminator.** I wrote one, and it was strictly better on its own terms — it repaired the one-line form too. It also changed two documented behaviours as a side effect of a fix aimed at a third. Discarded in favour of the one-expression change.
- **Asserting a count without a member list.** My first predicate — "a default that does not parse as a literal" — matched **213** doclets, most of them legitimate class-reference defaults like `model => "ColorModel"`. The real predicate is positional and yields 19. A ratio names one population; the table above names members so the next reader can re-derive rather than trust.
- **Testing a re-implementation.** The module's own docblock says it: *"A test that re-implements it cannot fail when this changes, which is the only way a regression here would ever be caught."* The spec imports the function.
